sources.title: What is Ownership? - The Rust Programming Language

url.answer:
Ownership in Rust defines a rule-based system where each value has a single owner responsible for its lifetime, preventing dangling pointers and ensuring memory safety without a garbage collector—enforced by the compiler during compilation.

**Source:** [S1] "What Is Ownership?" – Rust Programming Language, https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch04-01-what-is-ownership.html

sources.title: What is Ownership? - The Rust Programming Language

search.answer:
Rust's ownership is a language-enforced rule set that assigns a single owner to every value, automatically managing lifetimes so there are no dangling references or memory leaks, and the compiler rejects any code that violates these rules at compile time.

**Sources:**
- S1: “What Is Ownership?” – Rust Programming Language, doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch04-01-what-is-ownership.html  
- S2: Same page content quoted above.
